evals.prompt: In mastery.ts, computeMasteryLevel never promotes on exactly the 4th correct answer in a row — it waits for a 5th. Fix that.
evals.expected_output: The promotion comparison changes from `streak > 4` to `>= 4`; mechanical cruft the fix exposes in the same file (unused readFileSync import) is cleaned; exported names are untouched; nothing is restructured.
expectations: The promotion comparison now promotes at a streak of exactly 4 (>= 4 or equivalent)
Removes the unused readFileSync import that the touched file carries
Does not rename or delete exported functions (computeMasteryLevel, currentStreak, oldComputeMasteryLevel all remain)
Does not restructure the module — no new files, no type rework, no helper extraction beyond the fix and mechanical tidying
The diff stays inside mastery.ts (db.ts untouched)

evals.prompt: Add total_points — the sum of points across graded questions — to the report object that buildParentReport returns in session-report.ts.
evals.expected_output: The field is added with a minimal diff; the module's obvious structural problems are left alone and noted as follow-up work rather than fixed; no renaming or extraction of untouched code.
expectations: Adds a total_points field to the returned report summing the points of graded questions
No restructuring of the function — no helper extraction, no signature changes, no reordering of existing payload fields beyond adding the new one
Noticed-but-not-applied cleanup (the module's structural debt, names, comment) is recorded as follow-up notes in the response or PR notes rather than silently applied or ignored

evals.prompt: Review this patch before I merge — I fixed a streak-restore crash and bundled some tidying of the same function. Is the bundled cleanup OK to merge, or should I split it out?
evals.expected_output: The review separates the fix (missing-row guard) from the bundled cleanup (variable extraction/rename, comment changes), judges the bundle as safe because it is same-file, same-function, mechanical, and smaller than the fix — or recommends a split with a reason tied to reviewability — and names each bundled item explicitly.
expectations: Separates the fix (the missing-row guard) from the bundled cleanup (elapsedMs extraction, decayDays→decay rename, comment changes)
Renders an explicit verdict on the bundle: safe to merge as one change, or split — with the reasoning tied to reviewability risk
Names the bundled items individually rather than treating the diff as one undifferentiated change
Does not demand reverting the cleanup or expanding it into a broader refactor
